# Ignore the conventional plan filenames

## What

`.gitignore` carried `*.tfplan`. That pattern matches `something.tfplan` but not
a plan written to a name with no extension or a non-`.tfplan` suffix, so the
names `tofu plan -out=...` is most often pointed at were neither tracked nor
ignored.

Adds `tfplan*` and `plan.out` alongside the existing `*.tfplan`.

A plan file holds resolved variable values, so it belongs with the state and
tfvars patterns already in that stanza.

## Verification

`git check-ignore`, both directions:

```text
tfplan                IGNORED
tfplan.out            IGNORED
tfplan-ha-1215.out    IGNORED
tfplan.binary         IGNORED
plan.out              IGNORED
myplan.tfplan         IGNORED

main.tf               not ignored
outputs.tf            not ignored
variables.tf          not ignored
README.md             not ignored
```

`git ls-files | git check-ignore --stdin --no-index` returns empty, so no
currently-tracked file becomes ignored by the new patterns.

`*.tfstate`, `*.tfstate.*`, `*.tfvars` and `terraform.tfvars` were already
covered and are unchanged.
title: fix: ignore the conventional tofu plan filenames

## What

Syncs the `pbs` VM block in `deployment.json.example` to the current declaration shape:

- Template clone (`clone_template.template_id`) instead of ISO install — the `pbs` role in ansible-proxmox-apps installs the packages, so the guest is a Debian clone.
- DNS-first addressing (`dhcp: true`), matching every other declared VM.
- Both disks on the example's registered dual-parity bulk pool (boot 32 GB, datastore 1 TB) instead of `local-zfs` / an unregistered pool name; a `_pbs_comment` records that the datastore's durability constraint picks the node.
- Placeholder node moved from the R410 placeholder to the R710 placeholder whose bulk pool carries the backup role.

body:
## What

Removes two path entries from the apps domain in `roles/openbao_secrets/defaults/main.yml`, added in #654.

The read policy for that domain is rendered from the generating role's seeding map. Until that role converges, the paths carry no grant, and an ungranted read fails the whole secret fetch closed rather than yielding an empty value.

`optional: true` is deliberately not used here. That flag forgives a missing secret and still fails a missing grant, which is the correct distinction and stays as-is.

## Effect

`seed-keys.yml` is inert without these paths: the values render empty, both entries are rejected from the loop, and nothing is created. That restores the intended property that either half of the pair is safe to merge alone.

The paths are re-added in the same change that converges the generating half. The ordering constraint is now recorded in `seed-keys.yml`.

## Verification

```

Passed: 0 failure(s), 0 warning(s) on 45 files. Profile 'production' was required, and it passed.
```

# Move the prompt catalog pin to the triage query fix

The GitHub triage prompt named no query, so consecutive runs of the same job
composed different ones. One added a `labels` filter, which selects issues
carrying a label of that literal name — it returns an empty set rather than
erroring. Measured on one repository at one moment:

```text
issues?state=open                 -> 80 open issues
issues?state=open&labels=none     ->  0 open issues
```

That run reported **0 open issues** across the org and a delta of **685 → 0**,
six hours after the previous run reported 680 with per-repo backlogs.

The catalog fix is [ai-llm-prompts#51](https://github.com/dryvist/ai-llm-prompts/pull/51):
enumerate with `state=open` and nothing else, separate pull requests
client-side, use the identical query every run, and sanity-check a total against
the remembered baseline before posting — a total that has more than halved or
collapsed to zero is treated as evidence about the query first.

## Why the pin moves here

The workflow is already prescribed in the comment directly above this variable:

> A prompt edit lands in the catalog first; this pin then moves to that merge
> commit, so the converge is the only thing that changes what a job says.

This follows that literally. The previously pinned revision was the **immediate
parent** of the fix's merge commit, so this carries the prompt fix and nothing
else — no unrelated catalog changes ride along.

## Verification

Beyond the suite and lint, the pin was checked end to end rather than by
inspection:

- the pinned ref builds on the controller — the same `nix build` step the
  converge runs;
- the built artifact contains both new guards;
- the role's own frontmatter strip (`regex_replace('(?s)^---\n.*?\n---\n', '')`)
  was simulated against that artifact: both guards survive it, the body begins
  at the intended sentence, and no frontmatter leaks into the prompt the agent
  would receive.

`tests/hermes_agent`: **500 passed**. `ansible-lint`: **Passed**, 0 failures /
0 warnings, profile `production`.

## Scope

One pinned revision. No behaviour changes until a converge, which is the point
of the pin.

The memory-full condition observed on the same run is not addressed here — a
plausibility gate compares against a baseline, so that remains tracked
separately.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
title: fix(hermes_agent): move the prompt catalog pin to the triage query fix
